new.h1: B2B Marketing Agency That Fills [[Your Pipeline]]

new.q: What is B2B marketing?
new.a: B2B marketing promotes products and services to other businesses rather than consumers. It focuses on reaching decision-makers, building trust over longer sales cycles and generating qualified leads for sales teams. Typical channels are LinkedIn, search, content, email and account-based marketing.

new.q: Which channels work best for B2B marketing?
new.a: Usually SEO and content for research-stage buyers, LinkedIn for precise targeting by job title and company, and Google Ads for in-market searches. The right mix depends on deal size, sales cycle length and how your buyers research suppliers.

new.q: What is account-based marketing?
new.a: Account-based marketing (ABM) focuses marketing on a list of named target accounts. Each account sees tailored ads and content aimed at the people involved in the buying decision, so budget goes to the companies most likely to buy rather than a broad audience.

new.q: How do you measure B2B marketing?
new.a: We track qualified leads, meetings, opportunities and closed revenue through your CRM, not just clicks and form fills. That way your marketing pipeline is judged on the revenue it creates for your sales team, and budget can move to the campaigns that perform.

new.q: Do you work with our sales team?
new.a: Yes. GTech Digital agrees lead definitions, follow-up processes and reporting with sales from the start. We review lead quality together each month, so campaigns bring the kind of enquiries your team can actually close.

new.q: Do you need a contract?
new.a: No. GTech Digital runs B2B marketing on rolling monthly terms. B2B sales cycles are long, so we recommend six months to judge results fairly, but you can adjust scope or stop with a month's notice.

new.q: How do you approach B2B lead generation?
new.a: B2B lead generation starts with a clear ideal customer profile. We then combine SEO, LinkedIn and Google Ads to reach buyers at each stage, score leads, route them to sales within minutes and report on the revenue they generate, not just form fills.

new.q: What does a B2B marketing agency do?
new.a: A B2B marketing agency plans and runs the campaigns that create sales pipeline for business-to-business companies: lead generation, LinkedIn and search ads, account-based marketing, content and CRM reporting. GTech Digital works alongside your sales team and reports on meetings and revenue.

new.q: How much does a B2B marketing agency cost in the UK?
new.a: Most UK B2B agencies charge £1,500 to £6,000 a month in fees, plus ad spend. Fixed-scope projects such as a website or a lead generation campaign launch are quoted separately. GTech Digital gives a fixed quote after a free audit.

new.q: What is a B2B lead generation agency?
new.a: A B2B lead generation agency finds and qualifies potential customers for your sales team through ads, content, outreach and events. The best ones measure success by qualified opportunities and revenue rather than the raw number of leads.

new.q: Do you work with B2B companies outside the UK?
new.a: Yes. GTech Digital works with B2B companies worldwide, remotely from London by video call. We run multi-country LinkedIn and Google Ads campaigns, build account lists by market and localise landing pages and content. Fees are in pounds, and we also quote in other currencies for international clients.

new.q: How long does B2B marketing take to work?
new.a: Paid channels such as LinkedIn and Google Ads usually produce first qualified leads within weeks. SEO and content build over three to six months and then compound. Closed revenue follows your normal sales cycle, which is why we report pipeline at every stage.

new.heading: What Is B2B Marketing and How Does an Agency Help?
paras: B2B marketing is marketing to other businesses. Buying decisions involve several people, take weeks or months, and depend on trust. A B2B marketing agency reaches the right companies, helps every person on the buying team understand your value, and hands sales warm, qualified conversations rather than cold form fills.

The work combines demand generation (creating interest), lead generation (capturing it) and account-based marketing (focusing on named target accounts). GTech Digital measures all three in pipeline, opportunities and closed revenue inside your CRM, so marketing is judged on the same numbers as sales.

Many of our B2B clients sell beyond the UK. For them we run multi-market LinkedIn and Google Ads campaigns, build target account lists by country and region, and adapt content and landing pages for each market, all reported in one pipeline view.

new.h1: API and System Integration Services That [[Connect Everything]]

new.q: What is an API?
new.a: An API (application programming interface) is a set of rules that lets one piece of software request data or actions from another, securely and automatically. APIs are how your CRM, accounting, ecommerce and payment tools share information without anyone re-typing it.

new.q: Can you connect systems that do not have an API?
new.a: Often, yes. We can use database connections, file exchanges such as CSV over SFTP, or older SOAP services to integrate legacy systems. We then wrap them in a modern API so other tools can use the data safely.

new.q: Should we use Zapier or a custom integration?
new.a: Zapier and Make are great for simple, low-volume tasks. For high volumes, complex rules or business-critical data, a custom integration is more reliable and cheaper to run, because you pay for hosting rather than every task.

new.q: How do you keep integrations secure?
new.a: We use OAuth 2, encrypted credentials, least-privilege access and full audit logs, and follow UK GDPR rules for personal data. GTech Digital tests every integration against failure and abuse before it goes live.

new.q: What happens if an integration fails?
new.a: Failed messages are retried automatically and stored safely, and our team is alerted so nothing is lost. A dashboard shows every sync, so you can see what happened and replay any item that needs it.

new.q: Can you build an API for our customers or partners?
new.a: Yes. We build public and partner APIs with OpenAPI documentation, keys, rate limits and usage analytics. Customers and partners can connect to your platform safely, and you can see exactly how they use it.

new.q: Do you support integrations after launch?
new.a: Yes. We monitor integrations and update them when connected systems change their APIs, which happens often. Support plans include alerts, fixes and a named contact, so your data keeps flowing without surprises.

new.q: What is a REST API and why use one for third-party integration?
new.a: A REST API is the common standard that lets software exchange data over the web in a simple, predictable way. Most modern tools offer one, so third-party integration with systems like HubSpot, Xero and Shopify is faster, cheaper and more reliable than manual exports.

new.q: Do you deliver integrations for businesses outside the UK?
new.a: Yes. GTech Digital is based in London and builds integrations for clients worldwide. We work remotely in overlapping working hours, handle multi-currency and multi-language data, follow GDPR and international data protection rules, and host middleware in the cloud region you need. We also quote in other currencies.

new.q: How long does an API integration take?
new.a: A single connection between two systems with good APIs often takes a few weeks, including testing with real sample data. Larger integration platforms are delivered in phases, with a phased switch-over so your team keeps working throughout.

new.q: What is a headless CMS?
new.a: A headless CMS stores and manages content, then sends it to your website or app through an API. It keeps content separate from design, which makes sites faster and lets you reuse the same content across websites, apps and other channels.

new.q: Can we preview pages before publishing?
new.a: Yes. We set up live preview so editors see exactly how a page will look before it goes live, on desktop and mobile. Preview links can also be shared with colleagues for sign-off before anything is published.

new.q: Will we lose SEO when changing CMS?
new.a: Not if the migration is planned well. We keep URLs where possible, move metadata and set up 301 redirects for every changed URL, then monitor Google Search Console after launch so any ranking dip is caught and fixed quickly.

new.q: Can different people have different CMS permissions?
new.a: Yes. We set up user roles so writers, editors and admins see only what they need, with approval steps where required. Clear permissions keep your content accurate and protect the site from accidental changes.

new.q: Do you provide CMS training?
new.a: Yes. Every project includes team training and simple written guides, usually in one or two short sessions. Most editors are publishing confidently within a week, with a named contact at GTech Digital for any questions.

new.q: Do you support the CMS after launch?
new.a: Yes. Our support plans cover CMS updates, security patches, backups and new features, with a fixed monthly fee and a response time you can rely on, so your editors are never left stuck.

new.q: What are editorial workflows in a CMS?
new.a: Editorial workflows are the steps content passes through before it goes live, such as draft, review, approval and scheduled publishing. In a custom CMS we build these around your team, so every page is checked and nothing is published by mistake.

new.q: Do you build CMS platforms for businesses outside the UK?
new.a: Yes. GTech Digital builds CMS platforms for clients worldwide from London, running workshops and training by video call across time zones. We set up multilingual and multi-site content models, translation workflows, hreflang and global CDN delivery so every region publishes quickly. We also quote in other currencies for international clients.

new.q: Can one CMS manage several languages or websites?
new.a: Yes. WordPress Multisite, WPML and headless platforms such as Sanity, Strapi and Contentful can manage several languages or websites from one admin area. We model shared and local content separately, so each region edits its own pages while brand-wide content stays consistent.

new.a: Most tests run for two to four weeks, long enough to cover full weekly cycles and reach statistical significance. Stopping early can give a false winner, so we agree sample sizes and rules before each test starts.

new.q: Will A/B testing affect our SEO?
new.a: No. We follow Google's guidance for testing, using proper redirects and canonical tags, so your rankings are not affected. Faster, clearer pages often improve SEO as a side effect, especially when Core Web Vitals improve.

new.q: Which CRO tools do you use?
new.a: We use GA4, heatmap and recording tools such as Hotjar or Microsoft Clarity, and testing platforms such as VWO or Optimizely. We choose tools to fit your traffic and budget, and you keep ownership of every account.

new.q: Do you build the test variations?
new.a: Yes. Our designers and developers create and QA every variation, so tests are properly built, tracked and checked on every device before they go live. Winning changes are then rolled out for you on WordPress, Shopify or your custom platform.

new.q: Do I need to sign a contract for CRO?

new.q: What do CRO services include?
new.a: CRO services combine analytics review, heatmaps, user research and A/B testing, then turn the findings into a prioritised test roadmap. We also check Core Web Vitals and mobile usability, because slow or awkward pages quietly lose a large share of potential customers.

new.q: Do you offer CRO for businesses outside the UK?

We also quote in other currencies for international clients.

new.q: What is the difference between CRO and UX design?

new.a: Keep temporarily out-of-stock pages live with a clear message, a back-in-stock sign-up and alternatives. Redirect permanently discontinued products with a 301 to the closest match or category, so the link value and rankings they earned are not lost.

new.q: What is bleed, and why does it matter?

new.h1: UI/UX Design People Understand [[the First Time]]

new.q: What is the difference between UI and UX design?
new.a: UX design is how a product works: the steps a visitor takes, what they see first and whether they can finish what they came to do. UI design is how it looks and responds: layout, colour, type and the buttons they press. We design both together so the look supports the experience.

new.q: Do you design for both websites and apps?
new.a: Yes. GTech Digital designs websites, web applications and mobile apps, and we check that each design works on phones, tablets and desktops. Our UI/UX designers also work closely with our web and mobile app developers, so designs are practical to build.

new.q: How many people do you test with?
new.a: Usually five people per round, and most projects run at least two rounds. Five users reveal most of the common problems in a design, and each new round shows whether the fixes worked.

new.q: Can you improve an existing website or app?
new.a: Yes. We start by seeing how people use what you have now, find the points where they get stuck, and redesign those parts first. Every change is tested with users before it is built, so you only pay to develop improvements that work.

new.q: Will you hand the designs to our developers?
new.a: Yes. You receive the final designs, a design system and specifications the developers can build from in Figma. We can also work alongside your developers during the build, in person or remotely, to answer questions.

new.q: How long does a UI/UX project take?
new.a: It depends on the scope. A single landing page can take a few weeks and a full web application several months. We agree a timeline in the proposal before work starts, with research, design and testing milestones.

new.q: How much does UI/UX design cost in the UK?
new.a: A focused redesign of key pages usually starts from about £2,500, and a full web or mobile app design can be £15,000 or more. We give a fixed quote after a short discovery call, based on the number of screens, research and testing rounds.

new.q: What do I receive at the end of a UI/UX project?
new.a: Final designs for every screen, a clickable prototype, a design system with colours, type and components, and specifications your developers can build from. You own all the files, so you can use them with any development team.

new.q: What does a UX agency do?
new.a: A UX agency researches how people use a website or app, finds where they struggle, and designs and tests a better experience before it is built. User experience design covers journeys, information architecture, wireframes and prototypes; GTech Digital also designs the interface (UI) and hands developers ready-to-build files.

new.q: How much do agencies charge for UI/UX design?
new.a: UK agencies typically charge £650 to £1,000 a day for UI/UX design, so a focused website or app redesign often costs £6,000 to £20,000, and a usability audit from £2,500. GTech Digital fixes the price for an agreed scope after a free call.

new.q: Do you work with UI/UX clients outside the UK?

new.q: Is accessibility part of UI/UX design?
new.a: Yes. Accessibility is built into every UI/UX design project, following WCAG 2.2 AA guidance for colour contrast, text size, keyboard use, focus states and clear form labels. Accessible design helps every user complete tasks faster and widens the audience your website or app can reach.

new.heading: What is UI/UX design, in [[plain English]]?
paras: UI UX design is the process of making a website or app easy to use and clear to look at. UX (user experience) design is how a product works: the steps a visitor takes, what they see first, and whether they can finish what they came to do. UI (user interface) design is how it looks and responds: layout, colour, type and the buttons people press.

Good design is not decoration. It removes the questions that stop people buying, booking or signing up, and it follows WCAG accessibility standards so the product works for everyone, including people using screen readers or keyboards.

We run UI/UX projects for clients in London, across the UK and internationally. Remote research sessions and usability tests run by video call, so we can test with users in the markets you sell to, and we design layouts that work in several languages and currencies.

new.q: Is WordPress good for business websites?
new.a: Yes. WordPress is flexible, SEO-friendly and easy to edit, which is why it powers over 40% of the web. Built well, with a custom theme and few plugins, it is fast and secure enough for most businesses, from brochure sites to large content hubs.

new.q: Do you use page builders like Elementor?
new.a: We prefer custom Gutenberg blocks because they are faster and keep your design consistent. GTech Digital can still work with existing page-builder sites such as Elementor if needed, and tidy them up for speed and security.

new.q: Can you fix a slow WordPress website?
new.a: Yes. We remove unnecessary plugins, optimise images and code, add caching and a CDN, and fix Core Web Vitals issues. Most slow WordPress sites load two to four times faster after our speed work.

new.q: Can you fix a hacked WordPress site?
new.a: Yes. We clean the malware, close the vulnerability, restore from clean backups where needed and harden the site to stop it happening again. WordPress security is part of every build and every care plan we run.

new.q: Can you migrate our site to WordPress?
new.a: Yes. We move pages, posts, images and SEO metadata and set up 301 redirects so you keep your rankings. We test the new site on a staging copy and only switch over once everything has been checked.

new.q: Do you offer WordPress maintenance?
new.a: Yes. Our care plans cover updates, backups, security monitoring, uptime checks and small changes each month. You pay a fixed fee, so there are no surprise bills when a plugin or PHP update goes wrong.

new.q: Do we own the WordPress theme and code?
new.a: Yes. Everything GTech Digital builds for you is yours, including the theme, custom blocks and code. We keep it in your own version control with notes, so any competent WordPress developer can take it on.

new.q: Which PHP version should my WordPress site use?
new.a: Use a currently supported PHP version, which is PHP 8.2 or newer for most sites in 2026. Older PHP versions no longer get security fixes and run slower, so we test your theme and plugins and upgrade PHP safely as part of maintenance.

new.q: What does a WordPress development agency do?
new.a: A WordPress development agency designs and builds WordPress websites, custom themes, Gutenberg blocks, plugins and WooCommerce stores, then keeps them fast, secure and updated. GTech Digital builds without heavy page builders, so sites load quickly and are simple for your team to edit.

new.q: Do you build WordPress websites for businesses outside the UK?
new.a: Yes. GTech Digital builds WordPress sites for clients worldwide, working remotely by video call across time zones. We set up multilingual WordPress with WPML or Polylang, hreflang tags, multi-currency WooCommerce and global CDN hosting so every audience gets a fast, local experience. We also quote in other currencies for international clients.

new.q: Can WordPress handle a multilingual website?
new.a: Yes. WordPress handles multilingual websites well using plugins such as WPML or Polylang, with a separate URL for each language and hreflang tags so Google shows the right version. We also translate menus, forms and SEO metadata so every language version is complete.
